title: notifications-service latency spike — subscription-fanout deploy vs shared broker overload

ground_truth.summary: Deploy v2.7.0 introduced a subscription-fanout regression that quietly increased per-message publish overhead. Passive checks look compatible with either broker overload (H1) or the deploy (H2) — same shape as INC-4478, different service. The traffic-shift intervention shifts 5% of publish traffic back to v2.6.0. The old-version cohort recovers to baseline; the new-version cohort stays slow. Deploy confirmed. Rollback recommended. The verification signal (p95 publish latency on the canary cohort) recovers to within the band — this is the clean autonomous-success demo, distinct from INC-4478 by service, signal, and payload shape.

intervention_results._note_for_authors: THE CAUSAL TEST. Shift 5% of publish traffic back to v2.6.0 for 60s. Old-version cohort recovers to ~340ms baseline; new-version cohort stays at 2280ms. Cohorts diverge — deploy confirmed. Same pattern as INC-4478's traffic_cohort_split.

verification_result._note_for_authors: The canary cohort (routed to v2.6.0) recovers to 340ms — well within the 900ms band. Clean autonomous-success case: intervention fired, recovery verified, no human touch needed. Contrast with INC-4481 where recovery fails.
